seo.title: Homeless help in Houston - No Home Help
seo.description: Verified help in Houston for people experiencing homelessness: shelter, meals, showers, health care, benefits, jobs, ID, legal help, youth, veterans, and pets.

page.heading: Houston homeless and housing-crisis help
page.urgent: Immediate danger, fire, police, or ambulance: 911 Shelter, food, benefits, and local referrals: 211 or 877-541-7905 Mental-health crisis: call or text 988; Harris Center 713-970-7000 Domestic violence: 713-528-2121
page.notice: Beds, schedules, routes, costs, and eligibility can change. Call before traveling when possible. No listing guarantees a bed, meal, treatment, benefit, money, or job the same day. Call 911 for immediate danger or a medical emergency.
page.intro: If you are newly homeless, call 211 first. For housing programs, complete a Coordinated Entry assessment through a participating provider such as The Beacon, SEARCH, Healthcare for the Homeless, Star of Hope, or another Coalition partner. An assessment is not a promise of immediate housing. Tell the worker where you are, whether you are safe tonight, medical needs, age, children, pregnancy, disability, veteran status, pets, and whether you have identification.

entries.title: Emergency services — 911
entries.description:
Phone: 911.
Call for: immediate violence, serious injury, trouble breathing, unconsciousness, overdose, fire, or another life-threatening emergency. Give the exact location and describe the danger first.
City of Houston service guidance

entries.title: 211 Texas / United Way HELPLINE
entries.description:
Phone: 211 or 877-541-7905, free and available 24 hours; text: your ZIP code to 898211.
Use it for: current shelter, meals, food pantries, benefits, health care, domestic-violence help, rent or utility assistance, and other local referrals. Interpretation is available.
Ask the operator to verify: eligibility, intake time, documents, transportation, and whether a bed or appointment is actually available.
211 Texas / United Way HELPLINE

entries.title: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline
entries.description:
Call or text: 988, 24 hours.
Use it for: suicidal thoughts, emotional crisis, or concern about someone else. Ask for interpretation if needed. Call 911 when there is immediate physical danger or a medical emergency.
Harris Center crisis guidance

entries.title: The Harris Center 24/7 Crisis and Access Line
entries.description:
Phone: 713-970-7000 or 866-970-7000.
Service: mental-health crisis support, assessment, service access, and possible Mobile Crisis Outreach Team response for Harris County residents who can voluntarily accept help.
Immediate danger: 911.
The Harris Center — contact and crisis care

entries.title: Houston 311
entries.description:
Phone: 311 or 713-837-0311.
Use it for: city information, non-emergency service requests, municipal court information, and questions about a city department. For shelter and social-service placement, call 211.
Houston 311

entries.title: Street outreach
entries.description:
SEARCH Homeless Outreach: 281-994-9613; emergency: 911.
Service: outreach teams engage people living outside and may connect them with Coordinated Entry, health care, identification, benefits, shelter, or housing services.
Important: outreach is not an emergency response and does not guarantee transport or a bed. Give a precise location, description, and urgent health concerns.
Houston outreach contacts

entries.title: Project Access — free service transportation
entries.description:
Service: scheduled, no-cost transportation between participating homeless-service agencies and health centers. Tickets are distributed through partner sites.
Ask at: The Beacon, Lord of the Streets, Healthcare for the Homeless, or another participating provider for the current map, ticket, and boarding rules.
Project Access map and homeless-service directory

entries.title: Coordinated Entry — The Way Home
entries.description:
First step: call 211 or visit a participating access point. The Coalition itself does not provide walk-in services.
Service: a standardized assessment for possible referral to housing and supportive-service programs across Harris, Fort Bend, and Montgomery Counties.
Important: completing an assessment does not guarantee immediate shelter, rental assistance, or permanent housing. Keep your contact information current with the provider.
Coordinated Entry — Coalition for the Homeless

entries.title: The Beacon — Coordinated Entry access
entries.description:
Phone: 713-220-9737.
Published intake: Tuesday–Friday; sign up at day-center intake at 7 a.m.; first 25 people. Capacity is limited and service is not guaranteed.
The Beacon — get help

entries.title: Star of Hope — Men's Development Center
entries.description:
Phone: 713-227-8900.
Service: emergency shelter and recovery, education, employment, and case-management programs for men. Call first for current intake, identification, health, sobriety, and bag rules.
Current Houston shelter directory

entries.title: Star of Hope — women and single-parent families
entries.description:
Phone: 713-222-2220.
Published intake: Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–3:30 p.m., based on availability and first come, first served. Serves single women and single mothers or fathers with children.
Bring if available: ID, Social Security card, and one bag per person. Call even if documents are missing and ask what alternatives are accepted.
Star of Hope — women and families

entries.title: Salvation Army Center of Hope
entries.description:
Phone: 713-752-0677.
Service: supportive navigation shelter for single men and veterans, with case management and help addressing health, work, addiction, and housing barriers.
Before traveling: call for intake, bed availability, eligibility, and documents.
Salvation Army supportive navigation shelters

entries.title: Salvation Army Jones Family Residence
entries.description:
Phone: 713-650-6530.
Service: housing-navigation program for women and families, including case management, childcare, job skills, counseling, and referrals.
Call first: this is a program-based residence, not a guaranteed same-day walk-in bed.
Jones Family Residence

entries.title: Magnificat Houses emergency shelter
entries.description:
Phone: 713-529-4231, extension 1.
Published intake: appointment-based Monday–Friday; limited walk-in availability; beds are limited. Emergency stays are generally 14–30 days, with possible application for longer-term shelter.
Other help at intake may include: food, water, clothing, health-screening dates, ID partners, computer skills, and employment training.
Magnificat Houses — need assistance
entries.address: Intake location: 1410 Elgin Street, Houston, TX 77004

entries.title: Mission of Yahweh — women and children
entries.description:
Phone: 713-466-4785, extension 100.
Service: faith-based emergency and transitional shelter for women and children, with case management, counseling, classes, and help toward independence.
No walk-in guarantee: call for screening, interview, child-age rules, documents, and space.
Mission of Yahweh

entries.title: Open Door Houston — residential recovery housing
entries.description:
Phone: 713-921-7520.
Important: walk-in emergency shelter is not currently available. Doorway Recovery offers structured, program-based housing for men ready to enter recovery.
Call before going: ask about admission, fees, program rules, health requirements, and wait time.
Open Door Houston — current emergency services

entries.title: Covenant House Texas — ages 18–24
entries.description:
Phone: 713-523-2231; campus support is open 24 hours.
Service: free walk-in emergency shelter, drop-in help, parenting programs, and resources for young adults, including LGBTQ+ youth, pregnant youth, and young parents with children up to age 5.
Covenant House Texas

entries.title: Houston Area Women's Center — confidential shelter
entries.description:
Domestic-violence hotline: 713-528-2121 or 800-256-0551, 24 hours.
Service: safety planning and access to confidential emergency shelter for survivors of domestic violence. The public office address is not the shelter location.
Immediate danger: 911. Use a safe phone if your device may be monitored.
Houston Area Women's Center — contact

entries.title: The Beacon — breakfast and lunch
entries.description:
Phone: 713-220-9737.
Published schedule: Tuesday–Saturday; breakfast 7–9:30 a.m. and lunch 11 a.m.–noon. All services are first come, first served and can reach capacity.
The Beacon — current schedule

entries.title: SEARCH Resource Center — hot lunch
entries.description:
Published intake: Monday–Friday at 8 a.m. and Monday–Thursday at 1 p.m.
Services: hot lunch, showers, laundry, hygiene supplies, referrals, case management, employment, health clinics, and adult education. Call 211 or check the current resource card before a long trip.
SEARCH current resource card

entries.title: Lord of the Streets — weekday meals
entries.description:
Phone: 713-526-0311; hours: Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–noon.
Service: meals plus clothing, hygiene supplies, mail, phone, notary, health care, and referrals. Sunday worship and breakfast are at Trinity Episcopal Church, 1015 Holman Street.
Lord of the Streets — contact and hours

entries.title: Open Door Houston — community food distribution
entries.description:
Phone: 713-921-7520.
Published schedule: Monday–Saturday, 1–2 p.m. The organization states that meals for men are provided without paperwork; confirm before traveling.
Open Door Houston — meals and clothing

entries.title: Houston Food Bank — find nearby food
entries.description:
Food-help phone: 832-369-9390.
Service: current pantry, meal-program, and distribution locations by ZIP code. Call the pantry before visiting to confirm hours, identification, address rules, and supply.
Do not assume the Food Bank warehouse is a walk-in pantry. Use the map or helpline for the correct distribution partner.
Houston Food Bank — Find Food Map

entries.title: 211 food referrals
entries.description:
Phone: 211; text: your ZIP to 898211.
Ask for: an open meal today, pantry without proof of address, food delivery if you cannot travel, or benefits help. Give nearest cross streets if you have no ZIP code.
United Way 211

entries.title: Magnificat Houses meal-program transition
entries.description:
Phone: 713-529-4231.
Important: the former downtown Loaves & Fishes soup-kitchen location is temporarily closed while relocating. Meal service continues through Magnificat programs, but there is no confirmed public walk-in site or schedule online.
Call first: ask where a non-resident can receive a meal that day.
Magnificat Houses — current meal information

categories.title: Showers, laundry, mail, phones, and internet

entries.title: The Beacon — showers, laundry, mail, charging, and Wi-Fi
entries.description:
Phone: 713-220-9737.
Published schedule: Tuesday–Saturday. Private showers and full-service laundry are first come, first served. Pathways staff can also offer mailbox privileges, device charging, Wi-Fi, benefits connections, and referrals.
The Beacon essential services

entries.title: SEARCH Resource Center — showers and laundry
entries.description:
Services: showers, laundry, hygiene supplies, lunch, information, referrals, and case management. Intake times are published on the current resource card.
Ask before using SEARCH as a mailing address: confirm enrollment and pickup rules with staff.
SEARCH Resource Center card

entries.title: Lord of the Streets — mail, phone, clothing, and notary
entries.description:
Phone: 713-526-0311; Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–noon.
Services published: mailing address, mail pickup, local phone calls, clothing and hygiene kits, free notary, homeless letter, ID and birth-certificate referrals, bus help, and health-benefit screening.
Mail pickup requires valid ID. Enroll before sending mail there.
Lord of the Streets

entries.title: Salvation Army Young Adult Resource Center — ages 18–25
entries.description:
Phone: 713-752-0677.
Services: showers, lockers, laundry, hygiene supplies, clothing, phone, computer internet, mailing address, meals, shelter referrals, and ID assistance for young adults.
Young Adult Resource Center

entries.title: VA Community Resource and Referral Center — veterans
entries.description:
Homeless-veteran hotline: 877-424-3838.
Published hygiene hours: showers Monday–Friday, 8–11:30 a.m.; laundry Monday–Friday, 8–11 a.m. The center also connects veterans with housing, health, benefits, and work services.
Houston VA CRRC

entries.title: Houston Public Library — computer and internet access
entries.description:
Service: public computers use one-hour sessions and can be accessed with a library card or a Computer Use Only Card supplied by the library. Printing and downloading are available at sites, subject to local equipment and cost.
Ask staff: how to get computer access without permanent housing or photo ID and which branch is open. Do not leave personal accounts signed in.
Houston Public Library internet-use policy

entries.title: Medical emergency — 911
entries.description:
Phone: 911.
Call now for: overdose, unconsciousness, chest pain, severe breathing trouble, heavy bleeding, seizure, heat illness, or another life-threatening condition. Do not delay because of insurance or identification.
Healthcare for the Homeless emergency guidance

entries.title: Healthcare for the Homeless — Caroline Street Clinic
entries.description:
Phone: 713-286-6000.
Published hours: Monday–Thursday, 8 a.m.–4:30 p.m.; Friday, 8 a.m.–noon; no appointments from noon–1 p.m.
Services are free: medical, mental health, behavioral health, addiction counseling, pharmacy, dental, vision, well-woman care, HIV prevention, and care coordination. No insurance, ID, or proof of homelessness is required.
Healthcare for the Homeless locations

entries.title: Cathedral Clinic at The Beacon
entries.description:
Phone: 713-220-9730.
Published hours: Monday–Friday, 7:30 a.m.–noon; Saturday HOMES Clinic, 8 a.m.–noon. The clinic closes every afternoon.
Call before going: walk-in availability can change; Caroline Street Clinic also accepts walk-ins.
Cathedral Clinic information

entries.title: Reed Family Clinic
entries.description:
Phone: 713-532-9901.
Published hours: Monday–Thursday, 8 a.m.–4:30 p.m.; closed noon–1 p.m. and Friday.
Services: medical care for adults, women, children, and young people affected by homelessness or housing instability. No copay is charged.
Reed Family Clinic

entries.title: Harris Health open-access homeless clinics
entries.description:
Main homeless-health line: 346-426-0500; eligibility: 346-426-0702.
Call to choose the correct site: shelter-resident clinics have separate eligibility.
Harris Health Healthcare for the Homeless
entries.hours: Open-access sites include: Harmony House, Lord of the Streets, Navigation Center, and Open Door Mission. Services are open to people experiencing homelessness regardless of shelter status, by appointment and then first come, first served.

entries.title: Mobile medical and dental units
entries.description:
Medical van location: 832-547-4381; mobile dental: 832-986-0358.
Service: Harris Health mobile care for people experiencing homelessness. Routes change, so call for the current day, place, appointment, and eligibility.
Harris Health outreach services

entries.title: Houston Recovery Center — Sobering Center
entries.description:
Phone: 713-236-7830; open 24 hours.
Service: free, confidential, voluntary short-term monitoring for adults impaired by alcohol or other drugs who are ambulatory, non-combative, and medically stable, plus peer recovery referral.
Call 911 instead for: unconsciousness, breathing trouble, seizure, serious injury, severe agitation, or suspected overdose needing emergency care.
Houston Recovery Center — admissions criteria
entries.address: Address: 150 North Chenevert Street, Suite 100, Houston, TX 77002

entries.title: St. Joseph Clubhouse — ongoing mental-health recovery
entries.description:
Phone: 713-523-5958.
Who: adults with a current mental-health diagnosis who are under professional care. Membership is free and lifelong.
Services: peer support, structured work activities, meals, job readiness, wellness planning, and access to housing referrals and social services. Call to arrange intake or a tour.
St. Joseph Clubhouse

entries.title: Texas benefits help by phone
entries.description:
Phone: 211 or 877-541-7905; choose language, then option 2.
Help with: SNAP food benefits, Medicaid, CHIP, TANF cash assistance, Medicare savings, and case questions. Ask what can be used as proof when you have no fixed address or lost documents.
Texas Health and Human Services — benefits contacts

entries.title: Your Texas Benefits
entries.description:
Online service: apply for SNAP, Medicaid, TANF, Medicare savings, and other programs; upload documents; check interview dates and application status.
No device or internet: use a library, The Beacon, YARC, or Workforce Solutions computer. Sign out fully and do not save your password on a public device.
Your Texas Benefits

entries.title: Houston Food Bank Community Assistance Program
entries.description:
Helpline: 832-369-9390.
Navigators can help with: SNAP, TANF, Children's Medicaid, CHIP, women's health coverage, Medicare savings, and related state programs. English, Spanish, and interpreter support are available.
Appointment capacity can close temporarily: call for the current location or walk-in option.
Houston Food Bank benefits assistance

entries.title: Benefits and income support at The Beacon
entries.description:
Phone: 713-220-9737.
Service: Pathways staff can connect day-center guests with benefits, income supports, Coordinated Entry, mail, Wi-Fi, and partner programs. Arrive early because daily capacity is limited.
The Beacon Pathways services

entries.title: Lost Lone Star or Medicaid card
entries.description:
Lost or stolen Lone Star Card: 800-777-7328; Medicaid card: 800-252-8263.
Protect your PIN: never trade benefits for cash or let another person keep your card. Update your mailing address through Your Texas Benefits or 211.
Texas benefits card help

entries.title: SEARCH Employment Services
entries.description:
Services: job counseling, search, placement, training, veteran support, case management, GED preparation, and adult basic education.
Ask at Resource Center intake: what identification is needed and whether employment appointments are available that day.
SEARCH services

entries.title: Workforce Solutions — East End Career Office
entries.description:
Phone: 713-228-8848; hours: Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–5 p.m.
Free services: computers, Wi-Fi, printers, fax, resume and interview help, WorkInTexas search, accessibility technology, and possible training or childcare scholarships.
Workforce Solutions career offices
entries.address: Address: 4450 Harrisburg Boulevard, Suite 100, Houston, TX 77011

entries.title: Workforce Solutions — find the nearest office
entries.description:
Regional phone: 888-469-5627.
Houston offices include: Acres Homes, Cypress Station, East End, Northeast, Northline, Southeast, Southwest, and Willowbrook. Use the directory to confirm the current address and phone.
Find a Workforce Solutions office

entries.title: Magnificat Guest Advancement Center
entries.description:
Phone: 713-529-4231.
Services: computers and internet for job searches, resume and interview support, digital skills, workforce readiness, benefits connections, and other stability resources.
Call for access: services may be tied to intake, shelter, or Clubhouse participation.
Guest Advancement Center

entries.title: Star of Hope career and education programs
entries.description:
Women and families: 713-222-2220; men: 713-227-8900.
Services for residents: GED, resume building, job readiness, financial planning, life skills, and employment support. Ask whether any service is open to non-residents.
Star of Hope career and education support

entries.title: WorkInTexas
entries.description:
Service: official Texas job-search and workforce portal. Workforce Solutions staff can help create an account, search jobs, and prepare applications.
Job-scam warning: do not pay for an interview, check, gift cards, equipment, or a promised position. Verify the employer and written pay terms.
WorkInTexas

entries.title: Operation ID — referral-based document help
entries.description:
Phone: 281-833-3500.
Service: helps gather supporting documents, complete forms, and cover costs for Texas ID and birth certificates from any U.S. state, territory, or military birth abroad.
Referral required: no walk-ins or self-referrals. Ask your case manager at a partner agency such as The Beacon, SEARCH, or a shelter to submit a referral.
Operation ID — eligibility and process
entries.address: Organization: Main Street Ministries, 5100 Travis Street, Houston, TX 77002

entries.title: Beacon Law — legal help for people experiencing homelessness
entries.description:
Published intake: Friday; sign up when doors open at 7 a.m.; first 25 people. A partner case manager can also submit an application.
Cases may include: ID restoration, driver's-license holds, immigration-document replacement, name changes for ID, record clearing, Social Security appeals, and limited eviction help.
Beacon Law

entries.title: City of Houston birth certificates
entries.description:
Phone: 832-393-4220.
Published walk-in hours: Monday–Thursday, 8 a.m.–4 p.m.; arrive by 3 p.m. Capacity may close the line early. Fees and qualified-applicant rules apply.
If you lack money or supporting ID: ask a case manager for Operation ID or Beacon Law referral before paying an intermediary.
Houston Vital Statistics
entries.address: Address: Bureau of Vital Statistics, 8000 North Stadium Drive, Houston, TX 77054

entries.title: Texas state ID or driver's license
entries.description:
Service: Texas Department of Public Safety offices issue identification. Requirements depend on citizenship or lawful presence, identity, Social Security number, and Texas residency.
Before going: use Operation ID, Beacon Law, Lord of the Streets, SEARCH, or YARC to determine which documents and address letter are accepted. Operation ID funding does not replace the required DPS visit.
Texas DPS — apply for an ID card

entries.title: Lone Star Legal Aid
entries.description:
Phone: 713-652-0077 or 800-733-8394.
Service: civil legal help for eligible low-income clients. It does not handle criminal defense. Call or apply online and describe deadlines, notices, eviction dates, benefits, family safety, or disaster issues.
Lone Star Legal Aid — get help
entries.address: Houston office: 1415 Fannin Street, Houston, TX 77002

entries.title: Houston Homeless Court
entries.description:
How to enter: ask a participating homeless-service provider to sign you up; individuals do not enroll directly at a regular payment window.
Service: resolves eligible City of Houston misdemeanor offenses and warrants through alternatives to payment, including service-program activities, recovery meetings, computer classes, or job training.
Court information: 713-837-0311.
City of Houston Homeless Court

entries.title: Mailing address and homeless letter
entries.description:
Phone: 713-526-0311.
Services: mailing address, mail pickup with valid ID, homeless letter, free notary, ID or birth-certificate referral, and local phone use.
Enroll before using the address. Ask exactly how your name must appear and when mail can be collected.
Lord of the Streets social services
entries.address: Lord of the Streets: 3401 Fannin Street, Houston, TX 77004

categories.title: Women, families, youth, LGBTQ+, immigrants, and veterans

entries.title: Houston Area Women's Center
entries.description:
Domestic-violence hotline: 713-528-2121 or 800-256-0551; sexual-assault hotline: 713-528-7273 or 800-256-0661.
Available 24 hours: confidential safety planning, crisis support, and information about emergency shelter. Services are for survivors; call 911 for immediate danger.
HAWC crisis contacts

entries.title: Mission of Yahweh — women and children
entries.description:
Phone: 713-466-4785, extension 100.
Service: emergency and transitional housing for women and children. Call for interview, capacity, child-age rules, and required documents; do not arrive expecting a guaranteed walk-in bed.
Mission of Yahweh

entries.title: Covenant House Texas — ages 18–24
entries.description:
Phone: 713-523-2231; open 24 hours.
Service: free walk-in emergency shelter and drop-in support. The campus is LGBTQ+-affirming and has programs for pregnant young people and young parents with small children.
Covenant House Texas

entries.title: Asia's House — emergency shelter for ages 15–17
entries.description:
24-hour phone: 713-485-5520.
Service: voluntary, temporary emergency shelter for runaway or homeless youth ages 15–17 of all sexualities and gender identities, with case management and mental-health support. The shelter location is confidential.
No adult referral or signature is required to ask for entry. Call the 24-hour line or connect at a Grace Place Youth Night.
Asia's House — Grace Place

entries.title: Grace Place Youth Nights — ages 13–24
entries.description:
Call or text: 832-239-0824.
Published time: Monday, Wednesday, and Thursday at 6 p.m. No appointment is needed for food, hygiene items, and support for youth experiencing homelessness or housing instability.
Grace Place — get help
entries.address: Location: Living Mosaic Church, 2515 Waugh Drive, Houston, TX 77006

entries.title: Tony's Place — LGBTQ+ young people under 25
entries.description:
Call or text: 713-678-0733; email: info@tonysplace.org. — mailto:info@tonysplace.org
Services: case management, basic needs, support, groups, and a safe drop-in environment. The public street address is not posted; contact staff for location and current entry instructions.
Published drop-in: Monday–Friday, noon–2 p.m.; case management by appointment.
Tony's Place — get help

entries.title: The Montrose Center
entries.description:
Main phone: 713-529-0037; 24-hour sexual-assault helpline: 713-529-3211.
Services: LGBTQ+-affirming counseling, case management, anti-violence help, HIV testing, recovery support, gender services, youth programs, and community referrals.
Montrose Center services

entries.title: St. Frances Cabrini Center — immigration legal help
entries.description:
Phone: 713-595-4100; immigrant-rights hotline: 833-468-4664.
Service: free or low-cost immigration assessment, representation, citizenship help, services for crime victims, asylum seekers, immigrants, and refugees.
Fraud warning: do not pay a notario for legal representation. Confirm the provider is an attorney or DOJ-accredited representative.
Cabrini Center
entries.address: Address: 5599 San Felipe Street, Suite 300, Houston, TX 77056

entries.title: Catholic Charities — food, housing, refugee, and family referrals
entries.description:
Main phone: 713-526-4611; Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–5 p.m.
Programs include: food, housing or utility assistance, counseling, pregnancy and parenting, refugee services, employment, immigration legal help, and veteran services. Many services require phone or email appointment.
Catholic Charities — program contacts

entries.title: VA Houston — homeless veterans
entries.description:
National hotline: 877-424-3838, 24 hours.
Services: assessment, emergency or transitional housing referral, HUD-VASH screening, health and mental-health care, substance-use treatment, benefits, employment, and case management.
Bring any military information you have, but call even if documents are lost.
VA Houston homeless-veteran care

entries.title: BARC Low-Cost Wellness Center
entries.description:
Phone: 832-395-9084; appointments are required.
Services: low-cost microchips, core vaccines, heartworm testing, flea and tick prevention, and wellness packages. It is not a full-service clinic and cannot treat an owned sick or injured pet.
BARC Wellness Center

entries.title: BARC surrender and low-cost referrals
entries.description:
Service: pet surrender is appointment-based. BARC also lists low-cost spay and neuter partners; free assistance may be available through partner campaigns.
Before surrendering: ask 211, the shelter, and BARC about temporary foster, pet food, veterinary assistance, or a pet-safe placement. Capacity changes daily.
BARC frequently asked questions

entries.title: Pet and shelter intake
entries.description:
Tell the worker before accepting placement: species, size, temperament, vaccination status, carrier or leash, and medical needs.
Important: the Houston shelter directory does not guarantee that general shelters accept animals. Ask about a pet-friendly option or temporary care before traveling; do not abandon an animal to enter shelter.
Coalition shelter and service directory

entries.title: Verification and corrections
entries.description: This page was verified on November 11, 2026 using the Coalition for the Homeless of Houston/Harris County, City of Houston, Harris Health, Texas Health and Human Services, U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, and direct provider pages. Call first because daily capacity and intake rules change. If a service has closed or a detail is wrong, see how to submit a correction. — ../../CONTRIBUTING.md
